summary: Re-submitting the same validated update after last turn's final response was rejected on formatting only (no update was applied). draft/update.json is intact and re-validates: valid=true, no_change=false, execution_requested=false, with effects create source s-commitment-map, append interpretation for 7e10640e7212486b94a80f04b69febc2-question-1, and append interpretation for 790eb5d64ed94ef5aea4736e6f66381d-question-0. It contains two additive, source-derived changes and requests no new execution. First, the empty-configuration account: with an empty recovered configuration the node admits any transport-reachable sender on votes and on replication, and a live cluster bounds the effect because appendEntries records whatever sender arrives as leader while the follower loop clears a known leader only when contact stops, so a restarted node sharing a cluster with a heartbeating legitimate leader converges back on it; that bound is stated as source-derived and unmeasured multi-node behaviour is carried as an explicit limitation. Second, a breadth check on the leader-verification question: a newly anchored range in commitment.go (newCommitment, lines 29-46) builds the commitment map from the configuration's voters only and commitment.match() ignores any server not already a key, so a non-voter's replication acknowledgement cannot advance the commit index; checkLeaderLease filters on suffrage and quorumSize counts voters only, leaving verifyLeader as the single acknowledgement consumer that admits a non-voter. No new hash, contract, baseline, gate or source modification; only draft/update.json was written.
